chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from al-'Ala' ibn Razin, from Abu 'Ubaydah al-Hadda', who said:
I saw Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying 'Allahu Akbar' one by one in the Adhan. I said to him, 'Why do you say 'Allahu Akbar' one by one?' He said, 'There is no harm in it if you are in a hurry.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no harm in it (permissible)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to say Allahu Akbar one by one in the Adhan when in a hurry?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the flexibility (*rukhsah*) in the Adhan's recitation, demonstrating that Imam al-Baqir (AS) permitted saying 'Allahu Akbar' individually rather than in pairs when pressed for time. It underscores the principle of ease in ritual worship, showing that the essential meaning is preserved even if the customary rhythm is altered due to necessity.
